title: The Null Space Is a Line Through the Origin
topic: For the singular matrix M = [[1, 2], [2, 4]], the rows are multiples of each other so M is not invertible. Sweep a vector x along the direction d = (2, −1) and watch M·x stay glued at the origin — every point on that line is in the null space. Step x off the line and M·x jumps away from zero. The null space {x : M·x = 0} forms a subspace — here, the line through the origin spanned by d.

beats.narration: Some matrices squash a whole line down to a single point — the origin. Which vectors get sent there?

elements.content: Which vectors does this matrix squash to zero?

beats.narration: Take the matrix M with rows one two and two four. The second row is twice the first, so M is singular — it collapses the plane onto a single line through the origin.

elements.content: Coordinate grid; image-of-M line y = 2x shown faintly
Highlight the image line where every M·x lands
the image of M is a single line

beats.narration: Now sweep x along the direction d equals two negative one. As x moves up and down that line, M times x stays pinned to the origin — every one of those vectors lands on zero.

elements.content: Null direction line d = (2, -1) drawn dashed through origin
Image point M·x stays at origin (highlight)
every x on this line is in the null space

beats.narration: Step x off that line. Now M times x is no longer zero — the image point jumps onto the image line. Only the direction d sits in the null space; everything else is mapped elsewhere.

elements.content: Vector x sweeping in an arc OFF the null line
Image point M·x sliding along the image line

beats.narration: The null space of M is exactly the line spanned by d — a one-dimensional subspace of the plane.

elements.content: a subspace — line through the origin
